_general.hook: Why do dreams vanish minutes after you wake up?
points: They fade fast
Most dream memories are gone within minutes unless you rehearse them right away.
Moving makes it worse
Getting up and checking your phone pulls your attention away before the memory sticks.
The fix
Stay still, replay the dream with your eyes closed, then say or write it straight away.
_general.caption: Ever lose a dream the second you wake up? Here's why, and how to keep it. Do you remember your dreams? 👇

_general.hook: How to remember more of your dreams
points: 1. Decide before sleep
Tell yourself you'll remember a dream. It sounds silly, but intention helps.
2. Don't move yet
When you wake, keep your eyes closed and replay what you saw.
3. Capture it fast
Say it out loud or note it before you check your phone. Even one word helps.
_general.caption: Try these tonight and tell me if you remember more tomorrow 🌙

_general.hook: Having the same dream over and over?
points: You're not alone
Many adults report at least one recurring dream.
Look at the timing
Recurring dreams often show up around stress, change or something unresolved.
Track it
Writing them down shows when they come back and what was going on in your life.
_general.caption: What's your recurring dream? 👇 Mine is always being late for something.

_general.hook: Ever realised you were dreaming, inside the dream?
points: That's a lucid dream
You become aware you're dreaming, and sometimes you can steer what happens.
It's more common than you think
Many people have had at least one, often without trying.
A dream journal helps
People who record their dreams tend to notice dream signs, and become lucid more often.
